checks: At r=0 the area and bound vanish. At q=0 or q≥r/2 only nonnegativity is required. In the remaining range 0<q<r/2 and 1/2<a<1, q<ar so no empty-cap case is missed.

For q≤(1−a)r the excluded intercepts are q/a and q/(1−a), yielding r²−q²/[a(1−a)] in units of V. Above the middle vertex height the two retained edge fractions give (ar−q)²/[a(2a−1)]. At q=(1−a)r both formulas are (2a−1)r²/a. Open or closed cap boundaries have zero area.

Expanded the upper-branch square independently: its mixed term is −2a(4a−1)rq and the constant coefficient uses 1+8a(2a−1)=(4a−1)². On the lower branch r≥q/(1−a)≥2q gives derivative 2r−4q≥0, so comparison at the branch seam suffices.

At a=1/2 the excluded right triangle has area ratio 4q², giving difference (r−2q)². At a=1 the included triangle is a translate of (r−q)T, giving difference (r−3q)². These cases avoid the vanishing branch denominators.

At q=r/3 and 1/2≤a≤2/3 the threshold is at or below the middle height; a(1−a) decreases from 1/4 to 2/9, giving F≥r²/2 with equality at 2/3, including the seam. Scaling and the zero-radius case agree.

overlap.comparison: Ordinary simplex depth gives the same lower bound at (q,q) for r/3≤q<r/2, where the smaller barycentric coordinates are 1−2q/r and q/r. It gives only the orientation-independent 4r²/9 at the centroid, and does not furnish the angular bonus or the small-threshold envelope.

Its proof gives the exact triangle area tail for distinct vertex heights and handles repeated heights by a limit. Rescaling that tail gives the raw branch formulas used here. The comparison to the universal 4q(r−2q)₊ envelope for all q≥0 and the sharp restricted-normal coefficient are not stated there.
